Jordan (ACME): Hey team — after bumping max_batch_size to 256 on our embeddings route we're seeing big tail latency spikes (p95 ~4-10s). No 401s, requests return 200 but very slow. Happens intermittently under mixed small+large traffic. Example requests attached.

Jordan (ACME): ```python
# small single
client.embeddings([payload], model='open-embed-1536-v2')  # dim=1536

# large batch
client.embeddings([payload]*64, model='open-embed-1536-v2')
```

sam-support: Thanks — can you paste the exact model and sdk version? Any request IDs or DYNBATCH logs you can share?

Jordan (ACME): Model: open-embed-1536-v2, python-sdk 0.9.7. No auth errors. Sample logs from DYNBATCH after enabling debug:
```
DYNBATCH: coalesce_window_ms=10, max_batch_size=256
observed batch sizes: [1,64,1,1,64,64,2]
tail_latency_p95=4.8s
```

maria-eng-runtime: From that snippet it looks like a classic dynamic-batching priority inversion when max_batch_size is large. Small/high-priority requests are getting queued behind large batches because the scheduler is concatenating heterogeneous sizes and not preempting.

dmitri-eng-sre: I repro'd on staging with a short script that mixes small single-shot embeds and large 64-batch jobs. When the large batches hold the GPU for ~200-400ms each, the small requests queue up and p95 blows out. :eyes:

maria-eng-runtime: Immediate mitigations we recommend:
- Temporarily lower `max_batch_size` to 128 for the route
- Increase `coalesce_window_ms` to 25ms to give the scheduler a better view of small request bursts
- Enable `priority_slots` / preemptive slotting if you can (example: `priority_slots: {small: 0.25}`)
We'll prepare a runtime patch to support per-priority `max_batch_size` and preemption.

sam-support: Jordan — can you try the 128 + coalesce_window=25 change on your route and report p95/p99 after ~30m?

Jordan (ACME): Applied to route r-9b2. After ~30 minutes:
- p95 down to ~220ms
- p99 ~580ms
Still seeing occasional 1.2s spikes during heavy bursts but far better than before.

maria-eng-runtime: That's expected. The config change reduces head-of-line blocking. We're going to land a hotfix that enables per-priority batch caps + preemption so mixed workloads don't regress when max_batch_size is high. PR: https://github.com/redwood/rt/runtime/pull/4825
Plan: canary 5% tonight, full rollout tomorrow morning if stable.

sam-support: Also flagging this for docs/Kb — increasing max_batch_size can reduce unit cost but may increase latency under mixed-size traffic. We'll add a section for priority_slot examples and recommended coalesce windows.

Jordan (ACME): Thanks everyone — monitoring now. I'll DM sample request IDs and the DYNBATCH logs you asked for.
